answer: A stake-weighted reputation prism splits an agent's standing into verifiable facets — completed work, peer endorsements, and locked collateral — so one forged credential cannot fake the whole picture. New identities start with only a thin nectar allowance, earning fuller access through attested history, while a trust ripple lets honest peers vouch gradually. Forging one identity is cheap, but faking all three facets across many accounts costs far more than any single payout.
